 Jayson Tatum, Celtics stifle Mavericks in dominant performance: 9 takeaways
 The Celtics set a franchise record for a first-quarter lead, and they led by the widest margin seen in an NBA game after one quarter since 1987.
 Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum goes up to score during the first half of an game against the Dallas Mavericks on Nov. 15, 2026, in Boston. AP Photo/Mark Stockwell 
 By Tom Westerholm 
 November 15, 2026

 Jayson Tatum and the Celtics suffocated the Mavericks in their return to TD Garden in a dominant 131-94 victory that was over almost as soon as it started. 
 Here are the takeaways.
 Jayson Tatum salvaged his numbers organically 
 One of the myriad complimentary things that can be said about Tatum this year is that he hasn’t seemed concerned about his individual statistics, despite his newfound status as the Celtics’ unquestioned leader.
 The Celtics, who finished Sunday’s game with the best net rating in the NBA due to a top-five offense and a top-two defense, have been blowing out teams all year, and Tatum has gotten to put his feet up in a number of fourth quarters. He is currently 41st in the NBA in minutes played, sandwiched between Ayo Dosunmu and Jamal Murray, even though the Celtics boast the best record in the Eastern Conference. 
 Advertisement: On Sunday, Tatum was elite once again, and he finished the first half a staggering +28, but he was just 5-for-9 from the field with 11 points — Derrick White (more on him in a minute) was leading the way, and the Celtics were on track for yet another monstrous win. 
 Then, in the third quarter, Tatum took over. The Celtics were never seriously threatened, but he knocked down a jumper early in the period when the Mavericks forgot to cover him about 15 feet from the basket (which was par for the course for Dallas’ defense), and the floodgates fell open. Tatum hit several heavily contested 3-pointers, including one over a triple team to end the period, and he finished his evening with 32 points after a 21-point third quarter that trampled all over a Mavericks team that was concussed after one round but still had to finish the fight. 
 Advertisement: “Joe just kind of challenged us,” Tatum told reporters after the game. “Obviously it’s easy to really bring it when it’s a close game or things like that, but just trying to challenge our mindset of you’re up 25, 30, can you try to put the game away? 
 “I think we did a really good job of that today.”
 Stats, of course, don’t really matter in the grand scheme, but they matter to players who understandably would like to be considered for end-of-season awards, and they matter to fans who want their favorite players be recognized for their brilliance by others who might not catch every game. Celtics fans have long defended Tatum as one of the best players in the league, and he is — albeit a different kind of superstar than the likes of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokic, who stockpile extraterrestrial stat lines en route to MVP awards. 
 Tatum almost certainly will not win an MVP award this year if the Celtics keep putting teams away this early, but he deserves accolades of some kind, and a 32-point performance with six rebounds and six assists won’t hurt, even if it isn’t his primary aim on a team that he says has big goals.
 Advertisement: “At some point in training camp, maybe when we were in Charleston, it kind of clicked that we had something special,” Tatum said. 
 The Celtics’ defense is a chainsaw 
 The Mavericks did not look good in Sunday’s game, but to be fair, the Celtics also played one of the best defensive quarters you will ever see.
 For instance: How is anyone supposed to score when a defense moves like this?
 Yea I’m sorry Mavericks 
Not sure what they are supposed to do right now the Celtics are just way too connected on defense 
Boston leads 42-9 (yes that’s real) after quarter one pic.twitter.com/NHWTBAHGUO 
— Nik Land | NikNBA🏀 (@NIKNBAYT) November 15, 2026 
 Payton Pritchard started the possession by going under a screen before fighting his way over on a re-screen for Walter Clayton Jr. 
 The second screen freed Clayton a bit, but Baylor Scheierman was already lying in wait, having shaded over from Zaccharie Risacher, his own assignment. However, because Pritchard fought over the screen, he was able to abandon Clayton immediately and close out to Risacher. Sam Hauser did as well, and he stayed between Risacher and Naji Marshall, preventing a pass to the interior. Risacher dribbled toward the middle of the paint, where Scheierman feinted toward him, then flew back to Clayton when Risacher passed. Tatum left his man as well to double Clayton, who appeared to find an open shooter in the corner with Marcus Sasser, but Neemias Queta closed out and sent his 3-point attempt packing.
 Advertisement: The Celtics played the entire first quarter — and much of the rest of the game — on a string defensively, hounding the Mavericks into 12 first-half turnovers and 13-for-38 first-half shooting overall.
 “I thought in the first quarter, it was a little bit of, we were playing well, forcing them to take the shots we wanted them to take, and they missed some shots,” Joe Mazzulla said afterward. 
 Eventually, the Mavericks settled in a bit and started scoring, but the damage was more than done. The Celtics now have the second-best defensive rating in the league at 105.1, and they are starting to look better and better every game.
 Derrick White might be back on track 
 Don’t look now, but White scored 16 points and went 4-for-9 from 3-point range. He is shooting 41.9 percent from 3-point range in his last five games on 6.2 attempts per game, and he’s up to 34.
 White looks confident again from behind the arc, which could be quietly one of the biggest stories of the last two weeks for a Celtics team that badly needs him to return to his 2024/2025 levels of shooting. White is singularly good on the defensive end, and he’s scoring 1.22 points per possession on runners, according to Synergy Sports — if his 3-point shot comes fully comes around again, he is a borderline All-Star on a team that currently employs Tatum (who bumps up against the MVP conversation annually) and George (who is carving out a surprise All-Star case for himself as well). 
 The game was over almost immediately 
 Some blowouts produce scores that simply don’t look right, and the Celtics’ 42-9 lead after one quarter is a perfect example. 
 Advertisement: The Mavericks called their first timeout at the 7:14 mark after Jordan Walsh went on a five-point run by himself. At that point, the score was already 19-4. The Mavericks took a second timeout in the first quarter with 45 seconds remaining, presumably to give Dusty May an opportunity to lay into his team after Scheierman grabbed a steal and threw down a two-handed dunk that got the bench on its feet and produced the head-scratching 42-9 total. 
 The Mavericks reeled the Celtics back to a 24-point deficit in the second quarter, and they actually won the second quarter by three, but the first quarter made history — the Celtics set a franchise record for a first-quarter lead, and they led by the widest margin seen in an NBA game after one quarter since 1987. The Mavericks never seriously challenged the Celtics again.
 Sam Hauser has a new celebration 
 Hauser debuted a new 3-point celebration after one first-half 3-pointer. 
 If you like perfect 3-point form and high-arcing shots and aesthetically pleasing swishes and also mustaches, you’ll like this clip. 
 Sam Hauser's mustache celly is contagious in Boston 😂👨 pic.twitter.com/iYN97kZ5hL 
— NBA (@NBA) November 15, 2026 
 Hauser finished 3-for-4 from the field with a pair of 3-pointers and a pair of steals. Once again, he held up defensively as well — if not better — than we’ve ever seen in previous seasons. He is the Celtics’ plus/minus champion so far this season — his lineups are out-scoring opponents by a ridiculous 23.9 points per 100 possessions. 
 Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh excelled 
 Walsh is an interesting case for the Celtics — he is often credited with guarding the opposing team’s best player, but as he noted on Sunday, that responsibility actually belonged to Paul George, who took on Cooper Flagg and limited the Mavericks star to 17 points on 5-for-15 shooting.
 Advertisement: “I was kind of like more tasked with creating havoc with guys bringing the ball up the court,” Walsh said. “His kind of job was to kind of like contain him, and then obviously we shifted around him and tried to shrink the floor against him.”
 Walsh is a tough and willing defender, which is important for a player with his physical dimensions. 
 He also isn’t one of the Celtics’ better plus/minus players, despite frequenting the starting lineup. Even after Sunday’s beat down, his lineups are just +3.5 points per 100 possessions, 13 points per 100 possessions below the Celtics’ baseline, per Cleaning the Glass. 
 Scheierman, meanwhile, is on the opposite end of the spectrum. His lineups are out-scoring opponents by 16.2 points per 100 possessions, 6.7 points per 100 possessions better than the Celtics’ baseline, and his flair for the dramatic draws a lot of eyeballs.
 Beautiful outlet pass from Baylor Scheierman all the way down the court to Luka Garza
— Danielle H (@danielleceltics.bsky.social) 2026-11-16T00:48:08.641Z 
 Mazzulla lauded both players, as well as Hugo González, for their mentality. 
 “They just impact winning.” Mazzulla said. “They’re not distracted by any nonsense, and they understand that any night they could do something different that gives us a chance to win.”
 Devin Carter returned to the floor 
 In other good news, Devin Carter was available for the first time this season after a lengthy illness and a G-League stint. Carter, a former lottery pick who signed a two-way contract after an eye-opening preseason performance, played the entire fourth quarter and dished out an assist to go with a pair of rebounds.
 Chris Cenac is going to be ‘really really good’ 
 Chris Cenac believers, a group we are enthusiastically a part of here, were treated to a show in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Cenac played the final seven minutes of the game and threw down three massive dunks, one of which accounted for Carter’s lone assist.
 It's a Chris Cenac Jr. dunk contest in the 4th quarter whewwww
— Danielle H (@danielleceltics.bsky.social) 2026-11-16T01:05:07.545Z 
 Cenac, who predictably has been spending some time in Maine, has an incredible amount of raw talent, but don’t take our admittedly biased word for it. 
 Advertisement: “Chris is going to be good,” Tatum said. “Chris is good now. But he’s really, really going to be good.”
 What’s next 
 The Celtics are back in action on Monday at 7 p.m., facing the Magic at TD Garden. 
 They then hit the road again for a game against the Nuggets on Wednesday, followed by games on Saturday and Sunday against the Kings and Warriors respectively.
